subject: Control proxy rolling upgrade — observed connectivity lag and immediate action plan
messages:
From: Ayesha Khan <ops@medisys.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: Liam O'Neill <cto@medisys.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 200-500ms control proxy lag after today's rolling upgrade

Connor —

We started the rolling upgrade to the control proxy across our private VPC at 08:30 PT and immediately began seeing spikes in control-plane request latency from our side (200-500ms for handshake/keepalive). It looks like the agent heartbeats were queued briefly and a few inference requests timed out. Impact: 3 short user-visible delays across multiple regions (none lost persistent data, but user requests experienced retries).

What we have collected so far:
- Controller timestamps and agent heartbeats (attached: client-nettrace-20280623.pcap)
- A snippet of the server-side logs where we see the initial retry window (we can upload full logs on request)

We rolled back the upgrade at ~09:05 and the rate of incidents dropped, but we still see sporadic latency as of 09:40. Can you confirm whether Redwood performed any controlproxy kernel or config push that would match what we're seeing? Need to know what artifacts you want and whether we should keep the network traces.

Thanks,
Ayesha Khan
Platform Ops — MediSys Health
ops@medisys.com

Ayesha —

Thanks for the quick note and for attaching the trace. I’m escalating this right now to our on-call infra team and copying CS so we can coordinate status updates with your team. Initial answers:

- We did push a rolling controlproxy binary and a minor TLS config tweak to the private controlplane starting at 08:20 PT targeted to edge proxies only. The rollout window was 08:20–08:58 and our internal telemetry flagged a small increase in handshake latency on a subset of proxies at ~08:33.
- We are treating this as a rolling-upgrade regression and will prioritize rollback evidence & a temporary mitigation immediately.

Action plan for the next 120 minutes:
1) We’ll gather kernel-level and proxy logs (I’ll upload a tarball to the shared drive).
2) Can you confirm whether you kept the agent logs for one of the affected hosts (any host that shows repeated retry)? If so, please send one copy.
3) We’ll stand up a bridge at 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET (I’ll send calendar invite).

I will follow up with an internal summary in ~30 minutes and post the artifacts.

Connor O'Brien

Subject: Re: Intermittent 200-500ms control proxy lag after today's rolling upgrade

Team / Ayesha —

Quick engineering findings from the bridge and initial log triage:
- Root cause hypothesis: a throttling interaction between the new TLS session cache logic and our connection-reuse heuristics that, under certain timing patterns, introduces a micro-queue for handshake completion.
- Symptoms: short-lived control-plane request queuing (150–600ms) concentrated on proxies that handled >120 simultaneous agent connections during the window.
- Immediate mitigations we executed during the bridge: disabled the TLS session cache optimization for the next rolling batch and increased the handshake worker pool on affected proxies. We confirmed a drop in latency in our synthetic checks and your supplied traces.

Next steps (engineering):
1) Reproduce in staging under controlled simultaneous-connection load (INF-8721).
2) Build a small rollback patch that removes the session-cache code path and push as a hotfix if staging confirms.
3) Prepare a postmortem with timeline and artifacts — delivery ETA: 2028-06-24 EOD PT.

We’ll attach the proxy logs and the minimal hotfix candidate in the shared drive.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 24 Jun 2028 16:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-bridge summary, immediate remediation, and next steps (control proxy TLS session-cache regression)

Ayesha / Liam —

Thanks again for joining the bridge. Below is a concise summary and clear next steps. If anything is missing, flag it and I’ll update.

Summary of what happened:
- At ~08:20 PT on 2028-06-23 we rolled a controlproxy build that included a TLS session-cache optimization. Around 08:33 PT a subset of proxies experienced transient handshake queuing resulting in 150–600ms control-plane latency spikes observed by both Redwood telemetry and MediSys traces.
- MediSys rolled the upgrade and observed reduced frequency; Redwood enacted mitigation steps (disabled session-cache optimization and increased handshake worker pool) during the bridge which stabilized latency.

Impact observed:
- Short-duration user-facing delays (retries) but no lost persisted inference results. Total visible incidents: 3 brief retries across two regions.

What we changed immediately:
- Disabled TLS session-cache optimization on affected proxies (temporary revert).
- Increased handshake worker pool size to clear queued handshakes faster.
- Collected logs and PCAPs (attached) and created INF-8721 to track the engineering fix.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Hotfix candidate branch + test results: by 2028-06-24 20:00 PT (Vivek).
- Full postmortem with timeline, root cause, and preventive controls (including rollout gating and additional synthetic checks): by 2028-06-24 EOD PT.
- Offer: Redwood will provide a one-week increased monitoring window for MediSys (proactive alerts + dedicated on-call overlap) at no charge while we validate the patch in staging and during the next private deployment window.

Requested items from MediSys to close the loop:
- One representative agent log from an affected host (if still available).
- Confirmation that the transient issues have stopped in your environment after our mitigation.

Attachments included: controlproxy-20280623-logs.tar.gz, client-nettrace-20280623.pcap, connor-bridge-notes-20280623.pdf

We will follow up with the formal postmortem document and the Jira ticket references once the write-up is complete. Appreciate the quick collaboration here and apologies for the disruption.

Connor O'Brien
